## docs/api.md

Canonical source: [docs/api.md](docs/api.md)

﻿# Local HTTP API

This reference describes the local Python helper. Hosted [browser mode](docs/browser.md) uses an in-page adapter, not this service. The helper binds to `127.0.0.1` on port 8713 by default, or the next available port. `GPU_BENCH_PORT` changes the starting port; `GPU_BENCH_NO_BROWSER=1` suppresses browser opening. Keep this interface on a trusted local machine.

JSON errors have an `error` field. Invalid input and runtime conflicts generally return 400, missing runs 404, active-run edits or deletion 409, and unexpected failures 500.

State-changing requests must come from the helper's own browser origin, or an Origin-free local API client. Send JSON bodies with `Content-Type: application/json`; rejected cross-origin or non-JSON changes return 403. Authenticated model discovery must use POST; GET query parameters cannot select a credential environment variable. See [security](SECURITY.md).

## Read and control routes

Read endpoints are `GET /api/version`, `/api/env`, `/api/models`, `/api/status`, `/api/events?cursor=0`, `/api/runs`, `/api/runs/<id>`, `/api/runs/<id>/download`, `/api/preview?tokens=512`, `/api/export.json` and `/api/export.csv`. Pass the returned event cursor to subsequent polls. Exports accept comma-separated `ids`; without them they include all runs.

`POST /api/bench/start` accepts benchmark configuration and starts inference. `/api/bench/cancel` requests cancellation. `POST /api/runs/<id>/meta` changes label and notes; `DELETE /api/runs/<id>` moves a run to local trash; `POST /api/shutdown` stops Wattever. An active run cannot be edited or deleted. Benchmark runs write results.

Managed LM Studio additionally supports `POST /api/lmstudio/start` and `/api/lmstudio/unload`. Generic endpoints never use the LM Studio CLI to load or unload their models.

`POST /api/hardware/bandwidth` with `{}` measures storage → RAM and pinned RAM → VRAM while no benchmark is running. Optional `gpu_index` selects the NVIDIA sensor; `storage_probe_directory` chooses an existing folder on the storage volume to test (default: results folder). It returns `transfer_bandwidth` with capture time, raw samples, methods and explicit unavailable states. Native transfer probes also run automatically before throughput/capability benchmarks. Throughput start accepts the same private `storage_probe_directory` override. See [measurement methods](docs/measurements.md).

Include `run_id` to attach a later transfer profile to an existing benchmark. Hardware class and selected GPU/driver must match. The file is backed up, inference results stay unchanged, and metadata identifies the later capture time. This does not reconstruct historical transfer conditions.

`POST /api/bench/link` accepts `{"run_ids":["<managed-run>","<endpoint-run>"],"label":"Machine benchmark"}`. It groups stopped benchmarks on matching hardware/GPU/driver, with local inference explicitly asserted for generic endpoints. The first ID is the group root. Each run keeps its provider, settings and measurements; **Open machine benchmark** in Results selects all available members for charts, tables and multi-run JSON/CSV exports. Send all desired member IDs when updating a group. Files are backed up before group metadata is saved.

## Generic endpoint configuration

Use `provider: "openai"` for an externally managed streaming Chat Completions endpoint, including LM Studio used without CLI management. This integration uses an OpenAI-compatible transport subset; it does not implement the complete OpenAI API.

```json
{
  "provider": "openai",
  "endpoint_base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1",
  "endpoint_api_key_env": "BENCHMARK_API_KEY",
  "endpoint_inference_local": true,
  "models": ["<served-model-id>"],
  "sizes": [512, 5000],
  "concurrency_levels": [1],
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "repeats": 2,
  "reproducibility": {
    "quantization": "IQ3_S",
    "context_tokens": 32768,
    "kv_cache_dtype": "int8"
  }
}
```

Send this to `POST /api/bench/start` only when ready to run inference. Omit `endpoint_api_key_env` if authentication is unnecessary. Otherwise set that environment variable before starting the helper; the field contains only its name. Literal keys are rejected. URLs must use HTTP(S) without embedded credentials, query or fragment. A root URL gets `/v1`; an explicit API path is preserved. Do not supply `/chat/completions` or `/models` as the base.

`endpoint_inference_local` defaults to **false**, including for loopback addresses. Set it true only when inference executes on the benchmark computer. This user assertion permits local power attribution; neither route-origin detection nor a display name verifies server hardware.

`endpoint_reasoning_effort` defaults to null in the throughput API, which omits the request field. The UI defaults **Requested reasoning** to **None**. Set the API field to `none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high` or `xhigh` to request standard Chat Completions `reasoning_effort`. Unsupported requests fail visibly. The requested value is recorded separately from the engine's unverified effective behavior. Short budgets may otherwise end during hidden reasoning before a visible answer appears.

`token_limit_field` selects `max_tokens` (default) or `max_completion_tokens`. Explicit `temperature: null` omits that parameter; numeric values request the specified temperature, with UI default 0. Keep parameter choices consistent across comparisons. These are request controls, not verification of server behavior.

`POST /api/endpoint/check` accepts these connection fields and probes discovery without running inference. It returns `ok`, `models`, `manual_model_ids: true`, `provider`, resolved `endpoint_identity`, and an `error` on discovery failure. Exact served model IDs can always be supplied in `models`; discovery alone does not verify streaming inference or usage reporting. `GET /api/models?provider=openai&endpoint_base_url=...` is also available without credential forwarding; use POST for authenticated discovery and to keep connection details out of URL histories.

Discovered models preserve safe endpoint-reported quantization, context and state metadata. Managed LM Studio also uses its native model catalog to capture separately labeled `quantization_method` (QAT, QAD or UD when reported), with `quantization_method_source`. Result rows and optional quantization identity fields `method`/`method_source` retain these labels independently of the storage format. Older identities without method fields remain valid. When quantization appears only in a recognized model-ID suffix, `quantization_source` is `model_identifier`; explicit endpoint metadata uses `endpoint_reported`. An inferred suffix does not verify the served weights. Unknown quantization or context stays unknown. The UI uses a manual model ID only when discovery returns no models.

Results uses the current connection when discovering models for additional tests. With a generic endpoint, **Review new benchmark** opens the current served-model catalog and stages a separate run in Run; it does not modify historical measurements or start inference. Managed LM Studio retains same-file extension. Switching connection invalidates an open or cached model selection. Historical chart filters describe saved measurements, rather than the endpoint's current inventory.

The inference engine controls loaded models, context/KV allocation, quantization, placement, reasoning and speculative decoding. Effective generic settings use `context_policy` and `gpu_offload` of `provider_managed`, with no fallback reload. Result states such as `mtp`, `context_length` and `reasoning_disabled` remain unknown. A client context estimate does not prove the engine's context setting. Generic runs require reconnection and a new run; resume and same-file extension are unavailable. Cancellation aborts client work but cannot verify provider-side termination; a timeout stops the run for operator inspection.

Optional `reproducibility` fields are `engine`, `engine_version`, `model_revision`, `quantization`, `context_tokens`, `kv_cache_dtype` and `mtp_draft_tokens`. Results mark these `user_reported`. Optional `performance_claims` entries contain `precision` (`FP4`, `INT4`, `FP8`, `INT8`, `FP16`, `BF16`, `FP32`), finite non-negative `value`, `unit`, `kind` (`advertised_peak`, `measured`, `estimate`), `sparsity` (`dense`, `sparse`, `unknown`), `execution_path` and `source`. Source and execution path are required. Use `TOPS` for integer precision and `TFLOP/s` for floating point. These annotations stay separate from detected hardware and Wattever measurements; see [measurements](docs/measurements.md).

Endpoint URL, credential variable name and credentials are excluded from public results and exports. Connection configuration is not persisted for generic resume. Review public free-text labels, notes, model names and sources before sharing; see [security](SECURITY.md).

### Automatic endpoint identity

No endpoint label or public ID is required. Connect and direct API starts resolve them automatically. Optional `endpoint_name_override` supplies one public display name; leave it empty to use detection. Legacy `endpoint_id`/`endpoint_label` configuration remains accepted as an operator override.

Identity uses recognized official public cloud hosts or explicit service/backend metadata. Local/private `/health`, `/props` and `/version` probes are read-only and bounded by an overall deadline; unsupported probes fall back without guessing from ports or model aliases. Unknown software receives a **Local endpoint**, **Private endpoint** or **Remote endpoint** name. `endpoint_identity` records `id`, `label`, `source`, `service`, `version`, `location`, `route_registry` and `evidence`. Explicit service metadata is `detected`; recognized cloud hosts and the declared managed LM Studio provider are `inferred`; optional naming overrides are `operator_override`; unsupported detection stays `unknown`. Location describes the route origin, not verified inference hardware.

Canonical known public API routes use stable public provider IDs for community aggregation. Other routes, including custom paths on recognized cloud hosts, receive random opaque IDs stable for the operational base URL in a private local registry. The helper stores that mapping in ignored `results/.endpoint-routes.json`; browser mode uses local storage. URLs are neither hashed into public IDs nor included in public configuration fingerprints. Do not share the registry. Removing it or clearing browser storage can generate a new identity for a privately mapped route. A cloud provider label identifies the public service, not its underlying inference engine or weights.

Optional `canonical_model_id`, `model_source`, `reported_reasoning` and `reported_mtp` (`on`, `off`, `unknown`) describe the model separately. They feed `model_configuration`/`configuration_id` with endpoint identity; requested, reported and verified effective values stay distinct. Historical `user_reported` endpoint provenance remains supported. Hashes verify content consistency, not endpoint authenticity or actual served weights.

## Capability routes

Capability evaluation and validated imports are helper-only; hosted mode provides a shared read/export/compare library. It uses separate files and a sequential request protocol described in [capability evaluation](docs/capabilities.md).

| Route | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `GET /api/capabilities/suites` | Suite metadata, versions, digests and question counts |
| `GET /api/capabilities/status` | Running state, live item progress and available local telemetry |
| `GET /api/capabilities/events?cursor=0` | Bounded event stream snapshot and next cursor |
| `GET /api/capabilities/runs` | Capability run summaries |
| `GET /api/capabilities/runs/<id>` | Full saved run |
| `GET /api/capabilities/runs/<id>/download` | Public audit JSON download |
| `GET /api/capabilities/export.json?ids=<id>,<id>` | Public `capability_runs` bundle; omitted IDs selects all |
| `POST /api/capabilities/start` | Validate configuration, save run and start inference |
| `POST /api/capabilities/cancel` | Abort client work; provider termination remains unverified |
| `POST /api/capabilities/import` | Validate/re-score one run or a `capability_runs` bundle and save it |

`GET /api/capabilities/suites` also returns `runner` metadata from the running helper process: its `completion_policy`, generation/deadline `defaults`, and accepted `limits`. The UI requires a supported completion policy before launching or validating imports. An older helper can still expose saved results for browsing, but must be relaunched to apply updated capability code; refreshing browser assets alone does not update Python code.

Example start configuration:

```json
{
  "provider": "openai",
  "endpoint_base_url": "http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1",
  "model": "<served-model-id>",
  "suite_id": "gsm8k-test-chat-v1",
  "sample_size": 50,
  "repeats": 1,
  "seed": 0,
  "temperature": 0,
  "top_p": 1,
  "endpoint_reasoning_effort": "none",
  "max_tokens": 32768,
  "timeout_s": 0,
  "endpoint_inference_local": false
}
```

A model ID is required; endpoint naming/identity is resolved automatically for direct starts as well as the UI. `sample_size: 0` selects the full suite; a positive value selects a deterministic seeded subset, capped by suite size. Defaults are Core v1, 24 questions, one repeat, a 32,768-token total generation budget and no wall-clock deadline (`timeout_s: 0`), question-selection seed 0, temperature 0, omitted top-p and requested reasoning `none`. `send_seed` defaults false; true additionally sends `seed + repeat` to the generation API. Null top-p/temperature omit those parameters. Capability `token_limit_field` defaults to `max_tokens`; `max_completion_tokens` is an explicit alternative for endpoints requiring it. Unsupported parameters are visible failures, not silently retried with different sampling. The capability budget includes reasoning plus final output, and is independent of speed-test generation settings. `max_tokens` accepts 1 to 131,072; `timeout_s` accepts 0 to 86,400 seconds, with 0 meaning no wall-clock deadline. Stop remains available. Context and provider limits can still terminate generation. New evaluations record `completion_policy: "finished-stream-visible-answer-v2"`; the policy is part of the evaluation fingerprint. Historical runs without this field remain readable and retain their recorded decisions.

Only one speed or capability run may execute at a time; conflicting starts/imports return 409. Capability tests do not load/unload models for either provider. Local telemetry requires explicit `endpoint_inference_local: true` for both. An active request worker after timeout/cancellation continues to block new benchmarks. Import recomputes summary/grades from full audit answers and validates hashes; it does not authenticate the reported model or operator.

## Managed LM Studio configuration

The default provider is `lmstudio`. `LMS_BASE_URL` selects its API (default `http://localhost:1234`). For example:

```json
{"models":["<installed-model-id>"],"sizes":[512,5000],"concurrency_levels":[1,2],"max_tokens":256,"repeats":1}
```

| Setting | Default |
| --- | --- |
| `sizes` | 512, 5000, 10000, 20000, 40000 |
| `concurrency_levels`, `repeats`, `max_tokens` | `[1]`, 1, 256 |
| `gpu_offload`, `fallback_on_failure`, `stop_model_after_failure` | `max`, true, true |
| `context_policy`, `context_headroom`, `context_safety_fraction` | `per_test`, 512, 0.05 |
| `mtp_modes`, `warmup`, `disable_thinking` | `["off"]`, true, true |
| `load_timeout_s`, `per_test_timeout_s`, `power_interval_ms` | 900, 1800, 150 |
| `gpu_index` | 0 (telemetry sensor only) |

## Managed LM Studio extensions

`GET /api/bench/extend-plan?run_id=<id>` supplies extension options. `POST /api/bench/extend-plan` previews a selection such as:

```json
{"run_id":"<run-id>","model_modes":{"<installed-model-id>":["off","on"]},"sizes":[512,5000],"concurrency_levels":[1,2],"repeats":2,"retry_failed":false,"rerun_existing":false}
```

Optional booleans `fallback_on_failure` and `skip_after_timeout` control the new session's load-placement fallback and practical timeout skipping. Timeout-based skips are not hard capacity/OOM claims. Optional `per_test_timeout_s` sets the new execution session's timeout (integer 1 through 7200). Existing measurements retain their recorded budgets. `repeats` is the desired total per case (saved repeat count through 100). Raising it adds new slots. To repair individual cases, optionally supply `selected_cases` as a nonempty array of `[model_id, mtp_boolean, concurrency, target_tokens, zero_based_repeat]` tuples within the selected workload. For example, `[["<installed-model-id>",false,2,5000,0]]` with `rerun_existing: true` replaces only that first repeat. Omit `selected_cases` to use the full selection. Case selection applies only to the execution session; the benchmark keeps its full workload configuration.

Review counts and warnings before submitting the selection to `POST /api/bench/extend`. Defaults add missing cases; `retry_failed` includes failed and skipped cases; `rerun_existing` includes successful selected cases. Extension takes a history snapshot and modifies the existing file. `POST /api/bench/resume` with `run_id` creates a separate run for unfinished work. These operations load/unload models and require compatibility checks; see [measurements](docs/measurements.md) and [architecture](docs/architecture.md).

---

## docs/faq.md

Canonical source: [docs/faq.md](docs/faq.md)

# FAQ

## Can I run without installing Wattever?

Yes. The hosted [browser mode](docs/browser.md) connects directly to an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. The endpoint and browser must allow the connection. The Python helper also supports generic endpoints without LM Studio; managed model control and same-file extensions are specific to its LM Studio provider.

## Does the selected GPU determine where inference runs?

No. It selects a telemetry sensor. Configure placement in the inference engine and record the setup in notes. Generic endpoints require an explicit local-inference assertion before attributing client power to inference. See [measurements](docs/measurements.md).

## Are power numbers comparable?

GPU board and SoC rail measurements have different boundaries; estimated whole-system power is not a wall meter and only includes the selected GPU. Compare like sources and settings.

## Can I compare old and new files?

Older files remain readable. Compare protocol, model, corpus, settings, context planner and session provenance; legacy and newer context allocation can differ within an extended benchmark. See [measurements](docs/measurements.md).

## Does a failed case invalidate the benchmark?

No. Failures and skipped cases are recorded and can be retried. See [troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) for common causes.

## Must a benchmark be complete before I share it?

No. Partial sessions are useful contributions. Managed LM Studio runs can add missing cases to the same file later, subject to compatibility checks. Generic endpoint and browser experiments use new runs. See [sharing results](docs/sharing-results.md).

## Does any OpenAI-compatible API work?

The required surface is streaming Chat Completions. `/models` discovery is optional because you can enter exact served IDs manually. Missing usage counts leave generic token throughput unavailable. Responses, embeddings, image and audio APIs are not benchmarked. Configure context, KV cache, quantization and MTP in your engine; Wattever's generic adapter does not control them.

## Why can longer prompts show higher prefill throughput?

The displayed metric divides prompt tokens by client TTFT, which includes fixed overhead, queueing and network time. Larger batches can also use hardware more efficiently. Cache reuse and provider warm state can change it further. Inspect separately reported engine timings and cache usage; missing cache data does not establish a cold run.

## Does Wattever measure bandwidth and TFLOPS?

Hardware metadata includes reported memory clocks and PCIe link state where available. Its encoding-based PCIe ceiling is theoretical, and idle links can downshift. It does not benchmark DMA or memory bandwidth or derive compute peaks from GPU names. Optional sourced, precision-specific compute claims are user-reported and stay separate from detected fields. See [measurements](docs/measurements.md).

## Are GSM8K and ARC scores official benchmark results?

They use pinned real test splits, with versioned zero-shot chat prompts and deterministic numeric/answer-letter grading. They are Wattever adaptations, not published few-shot or likelihood-based leaderboard protocols. Compare matching suite/subset, token budget, sampling and grading versions. Public tasks may be contaminated, and repeats are not independent questions. See [capability evaluation](docs/capabilities.md).

## Does a configuration fingerprint prove which model ran?

No. It checks consistency of public model/endpoint identifiers and known/requested/reported settings. A canonical ID helps distinguish a served alias, but hashes do not authenticate weights or server routing. Unknown effective reasoning, MTP or quantization remains unknown.

## Must I invent an endpoint name or ID?

No. Connect resolves them automatically, as do direct API starts. Names come from recognized official cloud hosts or explicit service metadata, with generic Local/Private/Remote endpoint fallbacks when unknown. Ports and model names are not used to guess software. Advanced settings offer one optional **Display name** override. Canonical known public API routes have stable provider IDs; other routes use a private random-ID registry without publishing or hashing the connection URL.

## Can telemetry show thermal throttling?

It shows observed utilization, temperatures, clocks and power where sensors exist. Whole-run aggregates and recent history can reveal changes to investigate. Different workloads and competing processes also change these readings; drift alone does not diagnose throttling. The bounded recent trace may omit older samples while whole-run observed means/peaks remain preserved.

---

## docs/troubleshooting.md

Canonical source: [docs/troubleshooting.md](docs/troubleshooting.md)

# Troubleshooting

- **Hosted page cannot connect:** check the endpoint URL, server availability, CORS and your browser's local-network permission. HTTPS-to-localhost behavior varies by browser. See [browser mode](docs/browser.md).
- **Browser storage warning:** download the result JSON before closing the page; an in-memory result is lost on reload.
- **Helper endpoint discovery fails:** verify the API base URL and optional key environment variable in the helper's process. Use a root URL or API base such as `/v1`, not `/chat/completions`. Enter the exact served model ID manually if `/models` is unavailable. Run a small case to verify streaming inference; CORS is not required for helper-to-engine requests. See [API configuration](docs/api.md).
- **Endpoint name is generic or unexpected:** the service did not expose recognized metadata, or only route-origin information is available. A generic Local/Private/Remote endpoint name is valid and does not block inference. Connect again after correcting the URL, or set the optional advanced **Display name** override. No manual ID is needed. A regenerated ID after clearing local storage or removing the private registry is expected; keep URL mappings private.
- **Generic endpoint throughput is unavailable:** check whether the provider includes prompt and completion token usage in its stream. Wattever keeps throughput unavailable when those counts are missing; stream chunks are not tokens. Inspect `metric_sources` and `reported_timings` in JSON.
- **Generic power is unavailable:** local power attribution is disabled by default. Confirm inference runs on this computer before checking that assertion; a loopback proxy alone does not establish local inference. Remote server power cannot be measured by client sensors.
- **Generic endpoint context failure or timeout:** reduce the workload or adjust context/KV allocation in the inference engine. Inspect the engine after cancellation or timeout; client abort does not verify server termination. Reconnect and start a new run rather than resume/extend.
- **Helper timeout recovery stopped:** inspect LM Studio and ensure the model and requests have stopped before starting another run. See [measurements](docs/measurements.md).

- **LM Studio or models unavailable:** install LM Studio, run `lms bootstrap`, start its server and check that the models are downloaded. Verify `LMS_BASE_URL` if using a different endpoint. Reopen Wattever and check the Run page.
- **Power unavailable:** check `nvidia-smi` for NVIDIA sensors. On macOS, use the launcher and accept the optional power prompt; without authorization speed tests still work. Other sensors may not provide power. See [measurements](docs/measurements.md).
- **Load failure or context overflow:** reduce prompt size or simultaneous queries, inspect model context limits and available memory, or choose a smaller model. A failure is retained in results; use the retry option after correcting the cause.
- **Extension rejected:** extensions require managed LM Studio with matching hardware, selected GPU/driver, corpus and LM Studio version. Generic endpoints use new runs. Start a separate benchmark if compatibility changed or cannot be verified. See [sessions](docs/measurements.md).
- **No response from Wattever:** check the URL printed by its launcher and keep the server window open. The default starting port is 8713 but another available port may be selected. See [getting started](docs/getting-started.md).
- **Updated files but old UI or API:** finish active work, restart the helper and reload the page. `/api/version` includes a `build_id`; matching release numbers alone do not establish a matching build. The launcher preserves active speed/capability runs and can replace only an identified idle older helper. Use its printed URL; do not stop the model server to refresh Wattever.
- **Browser disconnect / WinError 10053:** a closed or aborted browser connection does not establish a benchmark failure. The helper handles disconnects while sending headers/body; reconnect and inspect saved status/results before starting another run. Update/restart an idle helper if its request handler still prints a disconnect traceback.
- **Capability parameter rejected:** select **Provider default** to omit unsupported `reasoning_effort`, or choose the token-limit field the endpoint supports. A changed request protocol is a distinct comparison. No visible answer after a short budget may mean hidden reasoning consumed it; inspect the run's usage/finish reason and adjust budgets fairly.
- **Capability import rejected:** use a finished full audit file with matching public configuration/suite/protocol/subset hashes and unchanged answers/grades. Redacted responses cannot be independently re-scored. Completed files need all planned observations; partial work uses cancelled/error/interrupted status. Do not repair hashes to conceal edited measurements.
- **CPU temperature unavailable or history starts late:** CPU temperature needs an actual supported sensor and can be unavailable while GPU temperature works. History retains the latest 3,600 points; check retention and all-run summary rather than interpreting absent samples as zero or no activity.

- **File-save warning:** review the warning's **Technical details** and retain downloaded JSON. For a managed LM Studio run, **Add / rerun tests → Add missing tests** can continue saved work after recovery. Generic endpoint runs start separately.

---

## CONTRIBUTING.md

Canonical source: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)

# Contributing

Share benchmark results by opening a pull request with one JSON file in `results/runs/`. The [sharing guide](docs/sharing-results.md) explains the GitHub upload workflow and how to add missing tests later. Review the file for information you do not want to publish and follow [results guidance](results/README.md). Record model builds, placement and relevant settings so readers can interpret results.

Capability contributions use individual `results/capabilities/<id>.json` files. Preserve full public audit answers, scorer decisions, suite/protocol/subset fingerprints and public configuration identities. Review prompts/expected answers and generated text before sharing. The helper's import independently re-scores and checks consistency; fingerprints do not authenticate execution. Keep dataset licenses/attribution and distinguish Wattever chat adaptations from official benchmark harnesses. See [capability evaluation](docs/capabilities.md).

For code changes, preserve old result readability, distinguish measured values from estimates, and document changes in measurement semantics. Wattever uses the Python standard library and local browser assets. See [architecture](docs/architecture.md), [API](docs/api.md), [changelog](CHANGELOG.md), and [security](SECURITY.md).

Run the software checks applicable to your change:

```sh
python -m unittest discover -s tests
node --check web/app.js
node tests/test_ui.js
node tests/test_endpoint_ui.js
node tests/test_browser_backend.js
node tests/test_capabilities_ui.js
node tests/test_tables.js
python tools/validate_results.py
python tools/update_docs.py --check
```

The optional browser test is `node tests/test_ui_browser.cjs`. State which platforms and real hardware you exercised; software tests cannot establish GPU performance. Follow the [code of conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md).

---

## SECURITY.md

Canonical source: [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)

# Security

The local helper rejects cross-origin state changes and non-loopback Host names. POST requests with a body require `Content-Type: application/json`; authenticated discovery uses `POST /api/endpoint/check`, not query parameters on GET. This prevents an unrelated webpage from asking the helper to forward named environment credentials. Command-line API clients without an Origin header remain supported.

Wattever serves a local interface that can start benchmarks, load or unload managed LM Studio models, and change local results. Keep it bound to loopback and use it only on a trusted machine. Generic endpoints receive your benchmark prompts and can incur provider charges; use a provider you trust.

The helper reads optional endpoint credentials from a named environment variable. Enter the variable name in Wattever, not a literal key. Endpoint URLs, credential variable names and credentials are excluded from public results and exports. They are not a substitute for reviewing free text: labels, notes, model names, reproducibility fields and compute sources are public annotations. Do not put secrets or private server locations in them. Browser-mode keys remain in memory; see [browser privacy](docs/browser.md).

Hardware discovery uses read-only, allow-listed OS/driver fields without elevation. It excludes serial numbers, GPU UUIDs, hostnames, network addresses and user paths. Inventory describes the benchmark client; it does not authenticate a remote inference server or verify its hardware. Local-inference attribution is an explicit user assertion. Review exported JSON before sharing, including older imported results that may contain legacy identifiers.

Capability audit files preserve exact public suite prompts, expected answers and source citations so their dataset digests and grading can be checked. Review those materials and generated answers before publication. Privacy-redacted responses cannot be imported as full independently scored audits. Public model/endpoint IDs must not contain connection locations or secrets. Content fingerprints establish consistency, not authentication or evidence that particular weights were served; see [capability evaluation](docs/capabilities.md).

Canonical known public API routes use stable public provider IDs. Other automatic identities use random public route IDs with private URL mappings in ignored `results/.endpoint-routes.json` or browser local storage. Do not publish those mappings. Connection URLs are not hashed into public IDs or result fingerprints. Service detection and route-origin labels are evidence about the connection, not verification of remote inference hardware or backend weights. Optional display names remain public annotations and need review.

Report suspected vulnerabilities privately to the repository maintainers through GitHub's private vulnerability reporting if available. Do not publish sensitive details before maintainers can respond. See [API](docs/api.md) for state-changing endpoints.

---

## CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md

Canonical source: [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

# Code of conduct

Treat participants with respect. Be constructive, welcome differing experience levels, and avoid harassment, discrimination and personal attacks. Maintainers may remove inappropriate contributions or limit participation to protect the community. Report concerns privately to the repository maintainers through GitHub. See [contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md).

## CHANGELOG.md

Canonical source: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md)

# Changelog

## Unreleased

- Measures sequential storage-to-RAM reads and pinned RAM-to-VRAM transfers before helper benchmarks, with raw samples, methods, capture time, unavailable states and UI/CSV reporting. Supports explicit later hardware-matched annotations on saved runs.
- Links engine-specific runs into one machine comparison while retaining each provider's settings and measurements.
- Captures generic endpoint quantization metadata in throughput result rows and accepts structured quantization formats during discovery.

- Adds total-repeat extension, adjustable retry timeouts and individual-test repair for managed benchmarks, preserving backups, successful measurements and replaced attempts. Managed requests honor the configured timeout; retry controls include explicit CPU-fallback and timeout-skipping policies.
- Captures quantization methods separately from storage formats, including LM Studio QAT, QAD and UD labels, and displays them before runs and throughout results. Catalog backfills retain explicit historical provenance.

- Discovers Results test models from the current authenticated endpoint, prevents stale selections after connection changes, and stages separate generic benchmark runs. Run and Results show quantization with endpoint-versus-model-ID provenance; successful discovery takes precedence over a manual fallback ID.

- Reports capability runner compatibility from the active helper process and blocks outdated launch/import flows with a relaunch message. Suite labels identify AI2 ARC-Challenge science questions separately from ARC-AGI; result headers show subset size, repeat count and descriptive uncertainty.

- Separates capability generation settings from speed tests, defaults to a 32k total thinking-and-answer budget with an optional deadline, and preserves completion metadata for empty final answers. Output limits remain distinct from request failures; new completion-policy fingerprints preserve historical audit compatibility.
- Aligns capability scorecards with a taller evaluation library, centers the workspace, and labels custom diagnostics separately from published dataset adaptations.

- Adds a visual capability dashboard with score/coverage tiles, category profiles, outcome breakdowns, repeat consistency and a filtered, paginated question-by-repeat matrix. An evidence inspector presents prompts, expected/actual output and rule explanations, with raw audit metadata collapsed. Compatible protocols support paired scored-answer deltas; live updates preserve filters and focus. Recorded scoring rules and protocol versions are unchanged.

- Resolves endpoint display names and stable opaque route IDs automatically from connection evidence, with honest generic fallbacks and one optional advanced display-name override. Manual endpoint naming is no longer required; private URL mappings stay outside shared results.

- Adds a capability evaluation tab with original Core tasks and checksum-pinned GSM8K/ARC-Challenge test splits, deterministic chat-adaptation grading, subset/repeat provenance, audit import/export and a read-only shared result library. These scores are separate from throughput and official leaderboard protocols.
- Adds public model/endpoint configuration fingerprints distinguishing requested, user-reported, verified and unknown settings, plus explicit reasoning-effort requests.
- Adds live CPU/GPU/RAM/VRAM telemetry and available temperatures, bounded recent history, whole-run observed means/peaks/coverage and descriptive early/late drift. Selected measures render in separate graphs.
- Identifies helper builds independently of release version, preserves active speed/capability runs during launch, and handles browser disconnects while sending response headers/body.
- Introduces browser timing protocol 2 with exact-usage-only throughput, explicit reasoning/output boundaries and public model configuration identities. Historical browser protocol 1 results remain readable and may include estimates.

- Adds generic OpenAI-compatible streaming Chat Completions to the Python helper, with optional discovery, manual model IDs, environment-based authentication and externally managed model settings. LM Studio remains a managed provider; generic experiments use new runs.
- Adds privacy-conscious CPU, RAM and PCIe provenance, optional user-reported reproducibility settings and sourced precision-specific compute claims. The additive metadata schema is version 1; benchmark schema 2 and historical files remain readable.
- Separates client timing provenance, provider-reported timings and cache usage. Generic throughput stays unavailable without server token usage; local power attribution requires explicit confirmation that inference runs on the benchmark computer.
- Excludes endpoint connection details and credentials from public results and exports.

- Keeps shared Results on GitHub-hosted catalog data, omits local execution diagnostics from public exports, and fails closed if the hosted data client is unavailable.

- Shows readable benchmark-save errors with optional technical details and refreshes shared data consistently after updates.

- Retains the latest RTX 5060 Ti session in the shared results library; removes older runs and preliminary snapshots.

- Adds a shared results catalog to the hosted Results view and a guide for contributing and continuing benchmark files.

## 2.4.1 - 2026-10-27

- Keeps viewport position and keyboard focus stable when toggling measures in Summary, Table and Compare.
- Includes a labelled preliminary RTX 5060 Ti result snapshot with its incompleteness and measurement limitations recorded.

- Preselects existing benchmark models when adding tests and shows each model's successful, failed, skipped and unfinished cases. New and unavailable models are distinguished; saved measurements remain intact when changing the selection.

## 2.4.0 - 2026-10-27

- Introduces measurement protocol 2, cross-platform hardware inventory, Linux support, concurrent queries and per-session provenance.
- Stores a benchmark in one JSON file and adds live case results, shared Results filters, chart comparisons and copyable tables.
- Adds same-file extensions, failed and skipped retries, selected-case reruns, attempt history and snapshots. Successful replacements remain separate from archived attempts.
- Plans shared KV capacity per concurrent request with a 5% prompt margin and supports a fixed context policy. Standard and MTP modes can be chosen per model.
- Adds hosted browser mode with direct OpenAI-compatible connections, local import/export and a separate measurement protocol.
- Adds adaptive request deadlines and verified model unload and worker recovery before continuing after a timeout.
- Adds a documentation set and an agent skill for the local API.
- Older concurrent failures may reflect legacy context allocation rather than a model capacity limit; use the session planner information when interpreting them.
- Older result schemas and planner settings remain readable. Extended files may contain sessions using different planners; compare provenance and settings before combining measurements.

## 1.0.0

- Initial release.

## results/README.md

Canonical source: [results/README.md](results/README.md)

# Benchmark sessions

This guide describes throughput files in `results/runs/`. Rule-scored capability
files are a separate result family under `results/capabilities/`; see
[capability evaluation](docs/capabilities.md) for their schema, datasets,
grading, public identities and independent audit import.

One benchmark is one JSON file in `runs/`. A session contains every model,
prompt size, concurrency level, repeat and failure measured for one machine
configuration. Changing cards or runtime GPU placement means starting a new
session. Historical unversioned files remain readable without rewriting them.

## Run and contribute

1. Launch Wattever, select a provider and connect. Generic endpoints support
   discovery or manual served model IDs. Managed LM Studio also supports **Reset
   for all models** to select downloaded models and restore standard settings.
2. Give the session a useful label, such as `RTX 5060 Ti - stock`. Choose prompt
   sizes and concurrent request counts. Default concurrency is one; click **10**
   to select all levels from one through ten. Prompt-length badges work the same way. Review the total request count.
3. With multiple cards, configure placement in the inference engine and describe it in the
   **Runtime GPU placement** field. The sensor selector controls power readings
   only. It does not change where the engine executes the model. For generic
   endpoints, explicitly assert local inference before attributing client power.
4. Run the benchmark. Failures and partial sessions remain useful data.
5. Download **JSON** in Results, or take the matching file from `results/runs/`.
   Review it for details you do not want to publish.
6. Follow the [sharing guide](docs/sharing-results.md) to upload the file and
   propose a pull request. Validation runs on the contribution and the shared
   catalog updates after merge. No index or aggregate file changes are needed.

## Standard format

New files use `schema_version: 2`. See [benchmark.schema.json](results/benchmark.schema.json).
Fields are additive; the existing `gpu`, `host`, `config` and `results` fields remain.
Additive inventory/run metadata uses `metadata_schema_version: 1`; old files
without it remain readable. Unknown data is not inferred from a model or GPU name.

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `application` | Tool version and measurement protocol version |
| `hardware.os` | OS name, release and architecture |
| `hardware.cpu` | CPU name, physical and logical core counts |
| `hardware.memory` | RAM module capacity, reported clocks and provenance where available; channel count/bandwidth stay unknown unless available |
| `hardware.system` | Manufacturer/model and physical RAM in bytes |
| `hardware.gpus` | Separate entries for every discoverable adapter; name, vendor, memory in bytes, driver and optional sensor index |
| `hardware.motherboard`, `hardware.firmware`, `hardware.storage` | Best-effort board model, firmware vendor/version and physical disk models/capacity/interface |
| `classification` | Hardware configuration grouping hash, GPU names and platform; not a unique machine identity |
| `measurement_scope` | Which GPU sensor supplies power and user-reported runtime placement |
| `provider` | Public provider label, managed/external model lifecycle and control boundaries |
| `measurement_client` | Client inventory kept separate when remote inference hardware is unverified |
| `reproducibility` | User-reported engine/version, model revision, quantization, actual context/KV and MTP draft settings |
| `performance_claims` | Sourced, user-reported compute claims with precision, execution path, sparsity and peak/measured/estimate classification |
| `model_configuration`, `configuration_id` | Public model/endpoint settings with requested/reported/verified/unknown provenance and a content-consistency fingerprint |
| `telemetry.history`, `telemetry.summary` | Bounded recent time series plus whole-run observed means/peaks/coverage and descriptive drift |
| `corpus.sha256` | Corpus fingerprint for comparing the exact workload |
| `config` | Selected models, prompt targets, concurrency levels and measurement settings |
| `results` | Measurements, failures, skips and cancellation records |

Unknown metadata is `null` or an empty collection. Hardware discovery is best
effort; an empty adapter list does not prove that the machine has no GPU.
New files omit GPU UUIDs, serial numbers, usernames and hostnames. User-entered
notes and runtime/model names are included; review them before sharing. Historical
files may still contain a GPU UUID; it may be removed without changing measurements.
Public outputs exclude endpoint URL, credential environment-variable name and
credentials. Review all free text, including labels, reproduction fields and
compute sources. Hardware describes the benchmark client, not verified remote
inference hardware. PCIe encoding ceilings are theoretical, not measured DMA or
device-memory bandwidth, and idle snapshots may downshift. Floating compute
claims use TFLOP/s; integer precision uses TOPS. See [measurement definitions](docs/measurements.md).
Public endpoint IDs/labels identify routes without connection URLs. Configuration
hashes do not authenticate actual served weights. Recent telemetry can drop old
points while whole-run aggregates retain observations; drift alone does not prove
thermal throttling. Missing temperature or utilization is unavailable, not zero.

## Concurrent measurements

Each result row includes `concurrency`; missing means one in historical files.
Single-request prefill/decode retain their original definitions. Groups above
one contain `requests`, including per-request status, TTFT and decode speed.
Each concurrent request has its own leading nonce to invalidate prefix caching.
In managed LM Studio, `lms load --parallel` sets prediction capacity for that
level. Generic endpoint concurrency and context capacity are engine controlled.

`aggregate_completion_tps` is successful requests' total output tokens divided
by group wall time, including prefill and queueing. It is not the sum of individual
decode speeds. A group is successful only when every request succeeds. Generic
endpoint throughput stays unavailable if server token usage is missing. Legacy
managed results can include explicitly marked stream-chunk estimates; the UI
marks estimated counts and derived throughput with `*`. Client prompt tokens/TTFT
is a prefill proxy including overhead, distinct from optional `reported_timings`.
Missing `cached_prompt_tokens` means unknown cache usage, not zero.
`timing_scope` distinguishes streamed content/reasoning from hidden reasoning and
`decode_token_count` records the scoped decode numerator. Reported unstreamed
reasoning is excluded; ambiguous hidden work can leave decode unavailable.

`group_power` covers the group interval. Concurrent phases overlap, so they do
not get invented prefill/decode energy splits. Power is for the selected GPU
sensor, never the sum of all connected cards. Whole-system power remains an
estimate and omits other GPUs' load; do not treat it as a wall-meter measurement.
Compare equivalent model/quantization, context, concurrency, offload, reasoning,
MTP, output budget, protocol and corpus before attributing differences to hardware.

## Local cleanup

**Results -> Delete** removes that session from the local application and
moves its JSON into ignored `results/.trash/`. Active runs must stop first. To
restore a session, move its archived JSON back into `results/runs/` and rename it
to the `id` inside the file plus `.json`, then refresh Results.

Deleting a tracked result produces a local Git deletion. This does not remove
the upstream copy; include only your new session file in a result contribution.

## Add, continue or rerun tests

These operations require managed LM Studio. Generic endpoint experiments require
reconnection and a new run; their public JSON does not persist connection details.

In Results, select a benchmark and choose **Add / rerun tests**. Select models and
their Standard/MTP techniques, prompt sizes and query counts. Choose an action:

- **Add missing tests** runs cases without a completed result.
- **Retry failed tests** includes failed and skipped cases as well as missing ones.
- **Rerun selected tests** includes successful cases too. Select one model to
  replace its measurements, or use **Select benchmark models** to select the
  installed models and techniques from the benchmark.

The preview separates new cases, failed retries, successful reruns and existing
measurements. Replacement is explicit; existing successful cases are preserved
when adding or retrying. Measurements use the same `results/runs/<id>.json` file.
Before execution, an exact local backup is written under ignored
`results/.history/`. Replaced rows move into `previous_attempts` with their
original session identifier, archive time and reason. Charts and summary medians
use active results, so replacements are not averaged with archived attempts.

`config` describes the benchmark's combined selections. Each item in `sessions`
records the settings used by that execution; result `session_id` links back to
it. `execution_config` is the most recent workload selection. This provenance
matters when extending an older planner run or adding MTP for one model.
`remaining_tests` counts requested cases with no terminal result.

Partial and completed benchmarks can both be shared. To add missing tests later,
use the same file and follow [sharing results](docs/sharing-results.md).
